title: The Bird That Says No

roles.sky: #9FB4C4 pale cyan-grey blue-hour window early, deepening to teal-slate #24474F by dusk; never indigo or violet
roles.horizon: #B89A9A dusty rose-grey warm-up at the ridge line, so lilac is the only violet in frame
roles.lamp: #FFE2A0 pale honey-cream lamp pool, lighting ONLY cold materials (chalk bench top, glass, steel, Nix's key side, the sill); never wood, never orange or ember
roles.ground: #4A4E52 neutral grey bench body and floor, #EEF0F2 chalk bench top, #2B2A30 soot charcoal coal refuse
roles.hero: #B8D433 lichen chartreuse canary felt, shade #7E9A1E, highlight #E4F27A
roles.accent: #B48CE0 neodymium lilac, ONLY rare-earth specks and a working flask's glow
roles.wall: #2F5DB8 cobalt, ONLY the scale wall and plant-scale dashed outlines; value target at least 25 L* darker than the cyan-grey sky behind it (wall L* about 40 vs sky L* about 72); against the dusk teal-slate the wall takes a pale cobalt rim #6D92DC so it separates; also the shot 10 corridor stripe as the wall's proxy
roles.whiteprint: #EEF0F2 chalk-white linework on #4A4E52 neutral grey for the PLANNED blueprint frame and the COULD frame; never a blue ground
roles.loss: #C8464A muted alarm red, ONLY ledger cells, the ledger page at the glass and the dial danger arcs; never at drape scale
roles.map: chalk paper #EEF0F2 land, #8C9196 neutral grey water, Canada a lighter grey #C9CDD2, four chalk-white pins with soot-charcoal rims (chartreuse stays Nix's alone), the dashed route ink, the $6M stamp in loss-red stamp ink

palette.mood: a curious, hopeful lab at blue hour: soft cold light outside, a warm bench lamp inside, a small bright bird against a big cobalt problem
palette.why: Lilac because rare earths (neodymium) ARE the lilac thing; chartreuse because the canary must pop and is the one living colour; cobalt alone owns blue, and blue means the problem. The field colour is a pale cyan-grey to teal-slate sky, NOT October 9th's indigo frost dusk and not 11-21's moonlit night; the ground is neutral grey so no second blue competes. Warmth comes from a honey-cream lamp on cold materials (chalk, glass, steel), not from 11-21's lamp-lit birch and walnut, and never ember or orange (October 9th's electricity colour).

light.S10_corridor: neutral grey fluorescent, the cobalt stripe the only saturated note.

shape_language: SMALL ROUND SOFT vs BIG STRAIGHT HARD: the canary, microbes, specks and flask are round and soft-edged; the scale wall and the plant-scale column are tall, straight, ruled and cobalt; the 200-step staircase is chalk-white paper, straight and ruled but never cobalt. The thesis is the size contrast.

casting.hero: Nix, NET-NEW reusable library asset (lib/canary.tsx): a lichen-chartreuse felt canary holding a two-faced card (NO on one face, OK on the other, plus a reticle face and FIX), moods, head snap, card flip, monocles, silhouette. Gap: the shelf has Raven, Puffin and Ptarmigan, none small, warm, or able to hold a card; a canary is the warning-before-harm idea itself.
casting.supporting_shelf: Suit (lib/people.tsx) for faceless Briggs, Heidari Kapourchali and the hard-hat worker, tie off; Stamp and FatArrow (kit.tsx) where a stamp or arrow is a plain mark; MotionBlur, ContactShadow, GradeLayer, HeldTravel, IdleFigure and FigureFinish from lib. Nothing else from the shelf: Thermometer, AnchorageSkylineBG, Moose, SteelVessel, TankFace, PowerGauge, AshHeap and FrostYardDusk are not cast.
casting.supporting_netnew_minor: Tier 1, reusable library assets in lib/canary.tsx, each with a reason: Nix (the hero, a small warm bird that holds a card; the shelf has no such bird), Microbe (a faced worker cast that any biology story can reuse), Flask (the throughline, glass with fill line and glow; no glass vessel exists on the shelf), ScaleWall (a cobalt block wall that grows; reusable for any 'wall' metaphor), Staircase (a stepped climb drawn to any count), GoalStool (the dashed four-or-five step stool, the film's scoreboard, chalk-white, round-cornered, outline-only by default), BenchWorld (a lab interior with a window that varies by seed). Tier 2, one-off shot props kept in lib/canary.tsx only because two shots share them: DataFeeder (frosted), Bassinet, BlockBar, GhostTank, Magnifier, Drum, ToyTurbine, TearCalendar, BlowPage. Tier 3 is the shelf list above. The depot Calendar is a slam calendar with a frost layer and does not tear off, so TearCalendar stays; Stamp from kit.tsx is used for the SKIPPED and NO RESULTS YET stamps.
casting.never: no SteelVessel or TankFace, no PowerGauge, no AshHeap, no FrostYardDusk (October 9th's cast); no faced metal fixture; real people faceless

motion_language: the world is quiet and cold, the bird is quick: Nix moves in snaps (head snap with overshoot, card flip with squash), microbes bustle in loops, specks drift and cluster on springs; the wall and the staircase GROW slowly and inexorably. 180-degree blur on the head snaps and the card flips; anticipation before each NO; specks overshoot into their cluster.

composition.focal_hierarchy: Nix or the flask is always the brightest, most saturated thing; plates sit high (y 560 to 690); the wall and staircase use the tall 9:16 frame
composition.negative_space: the dusk sky above the Chugach in the window is the breathing room after the test
composition.safe_area: hero action and plates inside y 420 to 1500 for the square crop; Nix's perch and the flask never below the caption top; the lower band is the bench front, glassware rack and floor
composition.signature_shot: Shot 14: in dusk silhouette Nix stands at the wall's foot beside the flask (lilac at half strength), aims a reticle card at the wall, chalk writes AUGUST 2030, the dashed GOAL stool slides out beside the chalk-white 200 paper steps on the Chugach behind, then a slow tilt up the dashed cobalt plant-scale column to the ridge against deep teal and a rose-grey horizon.

craft_advance: One reusable family, lib/canary.tsx, registered in ASSET_MANIFEST.md; no engine system advanced.
treatment: The Bird That Says No (Dramatist winner with grafts, restaged at Gate 0B). NIX, a lichen-chartreuse felt canary holding a card that turns between NO and OK, is the deep-learning model, a warning before harm, never a miner. S1 blue-hour lab bench at a window onto the Chugach: a lump of coal refuse thunks into an empty jar beside an empty flask with a blank neck tag; Nix snaps round, its card turning between NO and OK. S2 a faceless Briggs's magnifier hops rock to rock and finds lilac specks in every rock and across the whole range (not rare, per Briggs); specks fly into a motor and a toy turbine; one slips through his fingers, spread thin. S3 a paper staircase unrolls out the window up the Chugach past acid, heat and solvent drums; a faceless hard-hat worker with a hand truck sits down as the counter lands on 200. S4 the microbe crew tips a crumb of refuse into the flask and it blooms lilac (worked before, in the lab), then a cobalt wall rises behind it until it blots out the window. S5 a map table, Canada between Alaska and the lower 48, four pins and a dashed line, a $6M stamp spanning all four, a LED BY BRIGGS tag on Anchorage. S6 a cutaway: microbes squeeze scattered specks into a cluster. S7 a dashed GOAL stool, A HOPE, at the staircase's foot. S8 Nix lands among four dials; a faceless Heidari Kapourchali hangs a frosted DATA feeder, fill hidden, and wires each dial alive. S9 from above, a reactor row inside a PLANNED blueprint frame; Nix raises its card before the foam crests; a microbe spins the valve; FIX. S10 a corridor planner sheds months, a SKIPPED stamp inside a dashed COULD frame sends them flying back, a dashed arrow halts a third of the way up a cobalt stripe (SHOULD, per Briggs). S11 THE TEST: a cold street; Nix and the flickering flask stay on the sidewalk outside another building; its window lights on a dashed ghost pilot tank (DOE-FUNDED PILOT, DIFFERENT METHOD, 2023) and one red-stamped ledger page slaps against the glass. S12 that pilot's own dashed beaker and tank, its LAB bar 3 of 10 blocks taller than its PILOT bar, one feedstock. S13 night bench: a bassinet tagged THE FIELD rocks under a swinging lamp (still in their infancy); a reference feeder for neural networks in general caps at its line while a dashed to-be-gathered line draws on the frosted feeder and a dashed ? on the flask; NO RESULTS YET. S14 dusk silhouette at the wall's foot beside the flask: Nix aims a reticle card AT the wall (not over it), chalk writes AUGUST 2030, the dashed GOAL stool slides out beside the 200 paper steps, and the camera tilts up a dashed plant-scale column to the Chugach. S15 from inside the jar, Nix holds its card edge-on with 2030?, the flask's neck tag turns to AUGUST 2030, and a fresh lump drops in toward camera.
